You are agent_2, one of 4 agents (agent_1, agent_2, agent_3, agent_4) working together on one math problem.

## How you work
You call tools; they run in the order you call them, and you see their results in your next response. There is no turn limit. You stop by ending a response without calling a tool. If a teammate tags you, or replies in a thread you're in, after you stop, you are woken and carry on.

## Execution environment
You have your own Python scratchpad file, scratchpad.py: you can read, write, edit and run it. Each run is a fresh Python process, and may take up to 6 hours; while it runs you see nothing on Slack, and what it holds in memory is lost when it ends. A run may use 5 GB of memory in all and write files of up to 8 GB each, and it may use multiprocessing with up to 2 worker processes (no more: it is killed if it has more processes at once).
Next to it is workspace/, a folder the whole team shares: every agent's runs can read and write it, and what one writes there the others can use at once. Put code and results that others can reuse there (for example shared code in workspace/tools.py, or results in workspace/results.json), import shared code with `sys.path.insert(0, "workspace")`, and say on Slack what you put there. Don't overwrite a file someone else wrote: write your own.
The Python environment includes NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, NetworkX, pandas, scikit-learn, gmpy2, Z3, mpmath and SageMath. Sage is imported in the same interpreter (`from sage.all import *`), and GAP and PARI work through it; Sage's Singular-based multivariate ideal methods (such as groebner_basis) crash here, so use SymPy's groebner for those.
There is no public internet access or web search. Do not try to access websites, remote APIs, or install packages. A run cannot start other programs, except more Python processes for multiprocessing.

## Slack
The team shares one Slack channel, #proof. slack_post posts to it, or replies in a message's thread; write @name to tag a teammate. slack_read shows what you haven't read, and after each response you are told when something is waiting. The lead, a person, may post too.
Use the channel to work as a team: split the work, and claim a piece before you start on it so that nobody duplicates it; keep the discussion of one piece in its thread; post each result as soon as it is checked (what was shown, and where in workspace/ its code is); and tag the teammate you need something from.

For an integer \(t\ge 2\), consider all integers \(k\ge t\), finite sets \(V\), and families \(\mathcal F\) of \(k\)-element subsets of \(V\) with the following properties. The family is intersecting, meaning that \(F\cap F'\ne\varnothing\) for all \(F,F'\in\mathcal F\). Its covering number is \(t\), where the covering number is the minimum cardinality of a set \(C\subseteq V\) meeting every member of \(\mathcal F\).

In addition, choose a partition \(\mathcal F=\mathcal F_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\mathcal F_t\) into nonempty subfamilies and pairwise disjoint nonempty sets \(X_1,\ldots,X_t\subseteq V\) such that \(X_i\subseteq F\) for every \(F\in\mathcal F_i\). Define
\[
b(t)=\min\sum_{i=1}^{t}\bigl(k-|X_i|\bigr),
\]
where the minimum ranges over all the choices just described, including \(k\) and \(V\).

With \(\log\) denoting the natural logarithm, determine the exact value of
\[
\lim_{\substack{t\to\infty\\t\in\mathbb Z}}\frac{\log b(t)}{\log t}.
\]

The answer was proved recently, so it is not an open problem: your team's task is to find it and prove it, completely, and to write Python that really computes or checks every step that can be checked. Printing what you believe is not evidence. Arriving at an answer that settles less than the question asks (a partial or conditional answer, "not known") is not acceptable, and neither is conceding: when an approach fails, try another.

Proving it means showing that the answer is right in every case the question covers, and that no other answer is. Split the work, and the pieces of each part, between you on Slack.

Stop only when the team's proof is complete. Before you stop, post on Slack what you proved, and what is left.

Your conversation was compacted after it reached about 240k tokens (compaction 3): what came before your last few responses has been replaced by the handoff you wrote, below. Slack's history is all still there (slack_read with thread=<id> shows a whole thread, include_read=true the latest messages), and so are your files and workspace/.

## Main firm upper bound (MY duplicate-center construction)

Parameters \(m\ge2\), \(n>4m-1\). \(T=nm\) classes, \(m\) at each center \(a\in[n]\). Actual points \(E(K_n)\). Each class at \(a\) has all actual petals
\[
P\subseteq \mathrm{St}(a),\quad |P|=r=n-2m.
\]
Omitted centers \(O(P)=\{b:ab\notin P\}\), size \(2m-1\).
Targets \(L(P)\): ALL \(m\) classes at each omitted center. Thus
\[
\ell=m(2m-1),\qquad D_{\rm per}=r+\ell=n+2m^2-3m.
\]
Full members: own disjoint core \(X_i\), actual \(P\), one independently arbitrary point from EACH target core, **ALL choices included**.

Intersection:
- same class core;
- same center actual petals intersect since \(2r>n-1\);
- distinct centers: if petals don’t share bridge \(ab\), one omits it and targets ALL classes at the other center.

Huge cores \(c=T\): any cover <T exhausts no core, so only actual activation or own-core representative helps. Actual set \(A\) activates all \(m\) classes at center \(a\) iff \(\deg_A(a)\ge2m\); activated count \(m|Z|\le |A|\). Thus \(\tau=T\).
Retain ANY \(t\) classes of a \(T\)-class valid instance: cover number exactly \(t\), by adding representatives for omitted classes. Take \(n=m^2\), \(m=\lceil t^{1/3}\rceil\), get
\[
b(t)\le(3+o(1))t^{5/3}.
\]
Optimized \(n=4m^2\): \(T=4m^3\), deficit \(6m^2-3m\), constant \(6/4^{2/3}\).

from pathlib import Path
text=r'''INTEGER COMMON-DUMMY PHASE PARAMETER

Let t color classes have real vertices corresponding to NONEMPTY actual
sets of rank at most r, and one dummy vertex each. All dummies represent
the same fresh point. Define the symmetric disjointness coefficient D:
real-real is 1 for disjoint actual sets and 0 otherwise; real-dummy is
M, dummy-dummy is 0, and all diagonals are 0. Let
 Q(x)=1/2 sum_{v,w} D(v,w)x_v x_w,
with nonnegative mass summing to 1 in each color. Assume 0<M<1/4 and x
is a global maximum. Let R be total real mass. A color is mixed if both
its real mass and dummy mass are positive; pure-real if dummy mass 0;
pure-dummy if dummy mass 1. Suppose there is at least one mixed color.

CLAIM: delta=M(2R-t) is a NONNEGATIVE INTEGER.

Proof. Put B=J-D; on the supported color-zero-sum tangent space its
Gram form is positive semidefinite, since Q is maximal and J vanishes.
For a supported mixed real vertex S and its color dummy, u=e_S-e_dummy
has squared B-norm 2M. For any two mixed real vertices S,T, the inner
product of their corresponding roots is 2M if S,T intersect, and
2M-1 if they are disjoint. Cauchy-Schwarz excludes the latter because
1-2M>2M. Therefore ALL supported mixed real sets pairwise intersect.

For two supported real atoms A,A' in ANY pure-real color, the root
v=e_A-e_A' has squared norm 0 or 2. Its inner product with u is
1[A intersects S]-1[A' intersects S], an integer in {-1,0,1}.
Cauchy-Schwarz bounds its absolute value by 2*sqrt(M)<1, so it is zero.
Thus all supported real atoms of a pure-real color have the SAME
intersection status with S, regardless of their possibly fractional
masses. Each pure-real color has total mass exactly one.

The actual real-real disjointness degree of S is consequently the
NUMBER of pure-real colors whose entire supported actual family is
disjoint from S. No mixed color contributes, and no pure-dummy color
has real mass. This is a nonnegative integer. KKT equality between S
and its supported dummy gives
 degree(S)+M(t-R)=M R,
so degree(S)=M(2R-t)=delta, proving the claim.

BALANCED-HALL COROLLARY. If the underlying intersecting core family has
t classes AND covering number t, and all actual patterns have rank<=r,
then delta=0 is impossible when t>2r. Indeed every actual alternative P
in a mixed or pure-dummy color has real disjointness degree at most
delta by KKT. If delta=0, P intersects EVERY supported real set S.
Choose one such S, |S|<=r; it covers all mixed/pure-dummy classes. Cover
each pure-real color by one point of its own core, costing p additional
points. Since delta=0 gives R=t/2 and p<=R, this yields
 t=tau<=r+p<=r+t/2, hence t<=2r.

CAUTION: delta+1 arbitrarily chosen supported REAL ATOMS do not
necessarily have total weight>delta when pure-real colors have multiple
fractional atoms. The analogous covering argument needs atom WEIGHT
strictly exceeding delta; replacing weight by atom count is unsupported.

This phase integrality and delta=0 corollary do NOT give the missing
asymptotic bound. They strengthen the common-dummy global-QP structure
beyond arbitrary first-order nearblocker models.
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_common_dummy_integer_phase_proof.txt').write_text(text)
code=r'''from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations
from pathlib import Path
import sympy as sp,json
M=F(1,8);t=13
# Nine a/b colors (one has a nontrivial two-atom real mixture), one c,
# and three S={a,b} colors. Every color also has its common dummy.
fams=[]
fams.append([frozenset({0,1})]) # color 0: S
fams.append([frozenset({0}),frozenset({1})]) # color 1
fams.append([frozenset({2})]) # color 2: c
fams.extend([[frozenset({0})] for _ in range(4)])
fams.extend([[frozenset({1})] for _ in range(4)])
fams.extend([[frozenset({0,1})] for _ in range(2)])
assert len(fams)==t
vertices=[];colors=[];weights=[];index={}
for i,fam in enumerate(fams):
    for j,A in enumerate(fam):
        index[i,j]=len(vertices);vertices.append(A);colors.append(i)
        weights.append(F(1,6) if i in (0,11,12) else (F(1,2) if i==1 else F(1)))
    index[i,'d']=len(vertices);vertices.append(None);colors.append(i)
    weights.append(F(5,6) if i in (0,11,12) else F(0))
n=len(vertices)
D=[[F(0) for _ in range(n)] for __ in range(n)]
for a in range(n):
    for b in range(a):
        A,B=vertices[a],vertices[b]
        value=F(0) if A is None and B is None else (M if A is None or B is None else F(not A&B))
        D[a][b]=D[b][a]=value
assert all(sum(weights[j] for j in range(n) if colors[j]==i)==1 for i in range(t))
R=sum(w for A,w in zip(vertices,weights) if A is not None)
delta=M*(2*R-t);assert R==F(21,2) and delta==1
Q=sum(D[a][b]*weights[a]*weights[b] for a in range(n) for b in range(a))
assert Q==F(1057,32)
grad=[sum(D[a][b]*weights[b] for b in range(n)) for a in range(n)]
for i in range(t):
    supported=[a for a in range(n) if colors[a]==i and weights[a]>0]
    g=grad[supported[0]]
    assert all(grad[a]==g for a in supported)
    assert all(grad[a]<=g for a in range(n) if colors[a]==i)
# Exact GLOBAL optimum certificate via aggregate real masses A,B,C,S.
# Let a=A+B<=9,c=C<=1,s=S<=3 and z=a+c+s. Actual Q=AB+c(a+s).
# For z<=3: <=z^2/3; for 3<=z<=10: <=(z-1)^2/4+z-1;
# for 10<=z<=13: <=z+77/4. Adding M*z*(13-z) proves global maximum.
z=sp.symbols('z',real=True)
pieces=[z*z/3+sp.Rational(1,8)*z*(13-z),
        (z-1)**2/4+z-1+sp.Rational(1,8)*z*(13-z),
        z+sp.Rational(77,4)+sp.Rational(1,8)*z*(13-z)]
assert sp.diff(pieces[0],z,2)>0 and sp.diff(pieces[1],z,2)>0
assert max(pieces[0].subs(z,a) for a in (0,3))<sp.Rational(1057,32)
assert max(pieces[1].subs(z,a) for a in (3,10))<sp.Rational(1057,32)
assert sp.solve(sp.diff(pieces[2],z),z)==[sp.Rational(21,2)]
assert pieces[2].subs(z,sp.Rational(21,2))==sp.Rational(1057,32)
# Nontrivial pure-real norm-two root and three mixed norm-2M roots.
B=sp.Matrix([[sp.Rational(1)-sp.Rational(D[a][b].numerator,D[a][b].denominator) for b in range(n)] for a in range(n)])
def root(a,b):
    v=sp.zeros(n,1);v[a]=1;v[b]=-1;return v
roots=[root(index[1,0],index[1,1])]+[root(index[i,0],index[i,'d']) for i in (0,11,12)]
G=sp.Matrix([[(u.T*B*v)[0] for v in roots] for u in roots])
assert G==sp.diag(2,0,0,0)+sp.diag(0,1,1,1)*sp.Matrix([[0,0,0,0],[0,sp.Rational(1,4),sp.Rational(1,4),sp.Rational(1,4)],[0,sp.Rational(1,4),sp.Rational(1,4),sp.Rational(1,4)],[0,sp.Rational(1,4),sp.Rational(1,4),sp.Rational(1,4)]])
assert all(e>=0 for e in G.eigenvals())
for i in (0,11,12):
    S=fams[i][0];count=0
    for j in range(t):
        if weights[index[j,'d']]==0:
            statuses={bool(S&A) for A in fams[j]}
            assert len(statuses)==1
            count+=not next(iter(statuses))
    assert count==delta
result=dict(colors=t,real_vertices=sum(map(len,fams)),supported_vertices=sum(w>0 for w in weights),M=str(M),R=str(R),delta=str(delta),Q=str(Q),all_KKT_conditions=True,analytic_global_optimum=str(Q),gram=str(G),eigenvalues={str(e):int(v) for e,v in G.eigenvals().items()},nontrivial_pure_real_multisupport=True)
print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent2_common_dummy_integer_phase_checks.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_common_dummy_integer_phase_checks.py').write_text(code)
exec(compile(code,'workspace/agent2_common_dummy_integer_phase_checks.py','exec'))
